title.en: Lesson 1. ㅏ and ㅗ verbs take -아요

blocks.md:
### 💡 The Core Rule for -아요 / -어요
1. If the **last vowel of the verb stem is ㅏ or ㅗ** → **-아요**
2. For **all other vowels** (ㅓ, ㅜ, ㅡ, ㅣ, etc.) → **-어요**
3. `하다` verbs are the special exception: they always become **해요**.

blocks.why: The stem 가 ends in ㅏ, so it takes -아요. But 가 + 아요 contracts into **가요** rather than 가아요 — identical vowels merge.
“어제” means yesterday (past tense). 만나 + 았어요 contracts into **만났어요** instead of 만나았어요.
하다 is irregular and always becomes **해요**. The other three mean past (했어요), future (할 거예요), and desire (하고 싶어요).

blocks.say: 나는 오늘 친구를 만나고 영화를 봐요.
blocks.rom: na-neun o-neul chin-gu-reul man-na-go yeong-hwa-reul bwa-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud in a natural rhythm: “I meet a friend and watch a movie today.”

blocks.md:
### 💡 Verbs That Take -어요
- 먹다 (ㅓ) → **먹어요**
- 배우다 (ㅜ) → **배워요**
- 읽다 (ㅣ) → **읽어요**
- 기다리다 (ㅣ) → **기다려요**

If the last vowel is **not ㅏ or ㅗ**, it takes **-어요**.

blocks.why: The stem 먹 has the vowel ㅓ, so it takes -어요 → **먹어요**. 먹아요 wrongly applies the ㅏ/ㅗ ending.
The stem 배우 has ㅜ, so with -어요, ㅜ + 어 merges into **워** → **배워요**.
The stem 읽 has the vowel **ㅣ**. Since it is not ㅏ or ㅗ, -어요 attaches to make **읽어요**.

blocks.meaning: I wait for the bus for 30 minutes.
blocks.why: 기다리 ends in ㅣ. Combined with 어요, ㅣ + 어 contracts into **여** → **기다려요**.

blocks.say: 나는 매일 학교에서 한국어를 배우고 책을 읽어요.
blocks.rom: na-neun mae-il hak-gyo-e-seo han-gug-eo-reul bae-u-go chaeg-eul ilg-eo-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud connecting the three -어요 verbs naturally.

title.en: Lesson 3. Vowel Contractions and Combining Rules

blocks.h: How Vowels Merge Without a Final Consonant
blocks.md:
When a verb stem has **no final consonant (받침)**, the vowel of the stem merges with the ending **-아요 / -어요**.

Here are the most common contraction patterns in everyday speech.
Remember: stems with a final consonant (받침) do **not** contract! For example: **먹다** → **먹어요** (not 머요), **앉다** → **앉아요** (not 안자요 in spelling).

items.tip: I drink coffee now. — 마시다 (ㅣ) + 어요 → 마셔요
I watch television. — 보다 (ㅗ) + 아요 → 봐요
I write a letter in Korean. — 쓰다 (ㅡ) + 어요 → 써요

blocks.q: Match the dictionary form to its contracted 해요체 form.
Which is the correct present polite form of ‘오다’ (to come)?
blocks.why: 오 ends with ㅗ and has no batchim. ㅗ + 아 merges into 와, making **와요**. 오아요 is not contracted in standard polite speech.

blocks.meaning: I give a present to my friend at the cafe.
blocks.why: The stem 주 ends in ㅜ without batchim. In natural conversation, ㅜ + 어 contracts into 워 → **줘요**.

blocks.q: 마시다 (to drink) — Complete the sentence: 「아침에 물을 ___ .」
blocks.why: 마시- ends in vowel ㅣ without batchim. ㅣ + 어 combines into 여, so it becomes **마셔요**.

blocks.q: Arrange the words to say: “I watch a movie at the cinema.”
Read out loud: “I drink warm tea in the morning.”

title.en: Lesson 4. Distinguishing Confusing Pairs in Real Life

blocks.h: How to Choose the Right Ending Every Time
blocks.md:
Let's review the 3 steps to pick between **-아요**, **-어요**, and **해요**:

1. **Is it a 하다 verb?** → Always becomes **해요**.
2. **Look at the last vowel of the stem:**
   - **ㅏ or ㅗ** → **-아요**
   - **Any other vowel (ㅓ, ㅜ, ㅡ, ㅣ, ㅐ, ㅔ)** → **-어요**
3. Check if the vowels contract when there is no batchim.
Look closely at **살다** vs **열다** and **작다** vs **적다**! One vowel difference changes whether you attach **-아요** or **-어요**.

items.tip: I live in Seoul. — 살다 has vowel ㅏ → 살아요
I open the window. — 열다 has vowel ㅓ → 열어요
I work at the company. — 일하다 is a -하다 verb → 일해요

blocks.why: The stem 닫 has the bright vowel **ㅏ**, so it takes **-아요** → **닫아요**. 닫어요 uses the wrong vowel ending.
The stem 쉬 ends in vowel ㅟ, which is not ㅏ or ㅗ. Therefore it takes **-어요** → **쉬어요**.

blocks.q: Pair each verb with its correct ending category.

blocks.meaning: I listen to music in my room.
blocks.why: 듣다 has vowel ㅡ and changes ㄷ to ㄹ before vowels, taking -어요 → **들어요**.

blocks.q: 운동하다 (to exercise) — Complete the sentence: 「공원에서 매일 ___ .」
blocks.why: Verbs ending in -하다 always conjugate to -해요 in standard polite speech: 운동하다 → **운동해요**.

blocks.q: Read out loud smoothly: “On weekends, I exercise in the park and rest at home.”
